text:
maya: hey team — first week here, running into an odd MDM + FileVault issue on my MBP M2 (Ventura). I set up a dual-boot with Ubuntu for some infra testing. Kandji shows the DiskEncryption profile installed and escrowed, but System Settings reports FileVault: Off.

ben: huh. can you run `fdesetup status`? sometimes the UI takes a minute after a profile push.

maya: ran it, output below:
```
$ fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.
```
but our kandji dashboard says escrow key present and profile applied. KB implies enrollment should kick off FV.

it-support: thanks @maya. two quick calls: 1) dual-boot setups can modify the recovery or EFI layout and block automated enable. 2) Kandji may have pushed the profile but the user approval flow could be waiting in System Settings (look for a top banner). Can you paste `profiles status -type configuration` with any sensitive IDs redacted?

maya: sanitized snippet:
```
PayloadIdentifier: com.redwood.disk-encrypt
Status: Installed
UUID: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

karen: interesting — profile is installed but FV still off. We'll want a remote session to inspect whether the MDM can call `fdesetup enable` or whether macOS is refusing due to a nonstandard recovery path. Also check System Settings → General → Login Items for a Kandji helper prompt.

maya: I don't see any Kandji prompt app or banner. No popup came up during enrollment. Is it safe to let you enable FV remotely? I can approve a temp-admin session if needed.

it-support: before remote, run `diskutil apfs list` and `sudo /usr/bin/last reboot` and paste outputs. If disk layout looks normal we'll schedule a 30m session. Avoid modifying the EFI in the meantime.

maya: partial `diskutil apfs list` output:
```
APFS Container (1 found):
  +-- Container disk1  (synthesized)
  +-- Physical Store disk0s2
  |   APFS Volume Macintosh-HD - Data
  |   APFS Volume Macintosh-HD
```
no obvious third-party encryption or weird volumes.

ben: fwiw I've seen Ubuntu touch the ESP and move the RecoveryOS; if recovery is nonstandard `fdesetup` will often refuse until the recovery path is repaired.

it-support: ok @maya — please open a Lighthouse ticket titled "MBP M2 Ventura dual-boot enrolled but FileVault not enabling" and tag `it-support`. Include model, macOS version, that you dual-booted, and paste the outputs you ran. We'll triage and schedule a remote.

maya: filed: https://lighthouse.redwood.com/tickets/21456 — assigned to it-support. summary: "MBP M2 Ventura dual-boot enrolled in MDM but FileVault not enabled." Thanks y'all. :pray:

karen: once we remote in we'll either trigger FV via MDM or use a temp-admin flow for you to consent. Should be quick. Avoid additional installs that touch the bootloader for now.

kandji-bot: Disk encryption profile `com.redwood.disk-encrypt` verified installed; escrow key present.

it-support: leaving a note here for the ticket: probable recovery path mismatch due to Ubuntu; recommend remote repair and then re-run FV enable. We'll update ticket with steps and outcome.

maya: thank you everyone — appreciate the help! :heart:
